newsitem.title: USA: Apache assumes Mobil interest in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Apache assumes Mobil interest in Egypt.

text.p: Apache Corp said on Tuesday it reached an agreement to assume Mobil Corp's interests in three exploration concessions comprising 7.7 million acres in Egypt's Western Desert, adding to existing acreage there.
Apache said it would then hold an interest in a total of 19.3 million acres in Egypt.
The agreement, which would become effective January 16 with the approval of the Egyptian government, provides Apache a position in all four of the Western Desert's sub-basins, the company said.

Apache said it would assume a 50 percent contractor interest in the East Bahariya Concession, a 33 percent contractor interest in the West Mediterranean Block 1 Concession, and a 24 percent contractor interest in the NE Abu Gharadig Concession.

Apache President and Chief Operating Officer G. Steven Farris said: "These concessions significantly increase our acreage position in Egypt and enhance our exploration potential in the Western Desert."
The concessions carried a total drilling obligation of 11 wells over the next three years, the company said.

The acreage sits between Apache's Qarun and Khalda concessions, which are producing a combined 60,000 barrels of oil per day and are expected to exceed a combined 70,000 barrels by mid-1997, Apache said.
